about: The oral cavity as an anatomy textbook draws it: the lips and vestibule, the gums and teeth, the palate that roofs it, the tongue with its papillae, muscles and nerves, the floor and its folds, and two magnified diagrams (a taste bud and a molar). Only swallowing and vomiting are simulated, so the soft palate, tongue muscles and hypoglossal nerve carry those as display drives; taste, chewing, speech and saliva are not modelled, so every other part rests at its display anchor. Counts and sizes are schematic, and the taste bud and tooth are magnified diagrams, not true size.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Lips
parts.summary: Muscular folds that close the front of the mouth
parts.function: The lips are a ring of muscle (orbicularis oris) covered by skin outside and mucous membrane inside. They seal the mouth, take in food and drink and shape speech.

parts.label: Upper Lip
parts.summary: The upper fold of the ring that closes the mouth
parts.function: It meets the lower lip to seal the mouth and is marked in the midline by the philtrum groove. It takes in food and shapes speech.

parts.label: Lower Lip
parts.summary: The lower fold of the ring that closes the mouth
parts.function: It meets the upper lip to seal the mouth and holds in food and drink. It moves with the jaw in speech and chewing.

parts.label: Orbicularis Oris
parts.summary: The ring of muscle inside both lips
parts.function: This sphincter-like muscle closes and purses the lips. It lies between the skin outside and the mucous membrane inside.

parts.label: Vermilion Border
parts.summary: The red edge of the lips where skin meets mucous membrane
parts.function: It marks the change from the skin of the face to the thin, richly supplied lining of the lip. Its colour shows the blood close under the surface.

parts.label: Oral Vestibule
parts.summary: The slit between the lips and cheeks outside and the teeth inside
parts.function: It is the space that food passes through on its way in, and it is closed off from the cavity proper when the teeth are together. It is lined by mucous membrane that turns back onto the gums.

parts.label: Gingivae (Gums)
parts.summary: The mucous membrane that covers the tooth-bearing jaw bone
parts.function: The gingivae grip the necks of the teeth and cover the alveolar bone. They form a seal against the teeth.

parts.label: Hard Palate
parts.summary: Roof of the mouth: the bony hard palate
parts.function: The hard palate is a bony plate that separates the mouth from the nasal cavity. The soft palate continues it backwards.

parts.label: Palatine Rugae
parts.summary: Transverse ridges in the front of the hard palate
parts.function: The ridges of the mucous membrane help the tongue grip and press food against the palate.

parts.label: Incisive Papilla
parts.summary: A small bump behind the upper central incisors
parts.function: It lies over the opening of the incisive canal in the midline of the hard palate.

parts.label: Median Palatine Raphe
parts.summary: The midline ridge of the hard palate
parts.function: It marks the line where the two halves of the palate met in development.

parts.label: Soft Palate
parts.summary: The muscular flap behind the hard palate
parts.function: During a swallow it rises and seals the nasopharynx so food does not pass into the nose. It is also raised in vomiting for the same reason.

drives.note: During the swallow the soft palate is elevated to close the nasopharynx.
Vomiting lifts the soft palate to close the posterior nares.

parts.label: Uvula
parts.summary: The small tongue-shaped tip hanging from the soft palate
parts.function: It hangs at the back of the mouth and moves up with the soft palate when the nasopharynx is closed.

parts.label: Palatoglossal Arch
parts.summary: The fold running from the soft palate down to the side of the tongue
parts.function: This front pillar of the fauces marks the back of the mouth. It contains the palatoglossus muscle.

parts.label: Oral Cavity Proper
parts.summary: The space inside the dental arches
parts.function: It is bounded by the palate above, the tongue and floor below and the teeth in front and to the sides. It opens behind into the oropharynx through the fauces.

parts.label: Floor of the Mouth
parts.summary: The soft tissue under the tongue
parts.function: It is a muscular sling with mucous membrane on top and it carries the openings of the salivary ducts. It supports the tongue.

parts.label: Mylohyoid
parts.summary: The muscle sheet that forms the floor
parts.function: It stretches from the inside of the lower jaw to a midline seam and to the hyoid bone. It lifts the floor of the mouth during a swallow.

parts.label: Sublingual Folds
parts.summary: Ridges on the floor of the mouth beside the tongue
parts.function: They are raised by the sublingual glands lying beneath and carry the openings of their small ducts.

parts.label: Sublingual Caruncles
parts.summary: Small papillae either side of the frenulum
parts.function: The submandibular ducts open on each caruncle, so saliva from the submandibular glands enters the mouth here.

parts.label: Tongue
parts.summary: Muscular organ on the floor of the mouth
parts.function: The tongue is a mass of interlaced muscle carrying the taste buds. It moves food during chewing, pushes the bolus back to begin a swallow and shapes speech sounds.

drives.note: The tongue presses the bolus back against the palate to begin a swallow.

parts.label: Oral Part (Anterior Two-Thirds)
parts.summary: The part of the tongue that lies in the mouth
parts.function: It is the movable part that is seen when the tongue is put out. Its upper surface is covered in papillae.

parts.label: Pharyngeal Part (Posterior Third)
parts.summary: The part of the tongue that faces the pharynx
parts.function: It lies behind the terminal sulcus and forms the front wall of the oropharynx. It carries the lingual tonsil rather than papillae.

parts.label: Terminal Sulcus
parts.summary: The V-shaped groove that divides the two parts of the tongue
parts.function: It points back towards the foramen caecum and lies just behind the vallate papillae.

parts.label: Foramen Caecum
parts.summary: A small pit at the point of the terminal sulcus
parts.function: It marks where the thyroid gland began in the embryo.

parts.label: Median Sulcus
parts.summary: The groove down the middle of the upper surface
parts.function: It divides the tongue into right and left halves.

parts.label: Lingual Frenulum
parts.summary: The fold that joins the underside of the tongue to the floor of the mouth
parts.function: It steadies the tongue in the midline while leaving the tip free to move.

parts.label: Filiform Papillae
parts.summary: The numerous fine conical projections of the tongue surface
parts.function: They give the surface its roughness for gripping food. They do not carry taste buds.

parts.label: Fungiform Papillae
parts.summary: Mushroom-shaped red papillae scattered among the filiform ones
parts.function: They are most common at the tip and sides and carry taste buds on their upper surface.

parts.label: Foliate Papillae
parts.summary: Folds on the sides of the back of the tongue
parts.function: They carry taste buds in the walls of their grooves.

parts.label: Vallate Papillae
parts.summary: The large papillae in a row in front of the terminal sulcus
parts.function: Each sits in a trench and has taste buds in its walls. Small glands empty into the trench.

parts.label: Taste Buds of the Vallate Papillae
parts.summary: Taste receptors in the walls of the trench
parts.function: They sense the chemical qualities of dissolved food. They are drawn here as small beads and are shown magnified in the Taste Bud entry.

parts.label: Intrinsic Muscles
parts.summary: The muscle fibres that lie wholly inside the tongue
parts.function: Longitudinal, transverse and vertical fibres change the shape of the tongue. They shorten, flatten, narrow and curl it.

drives.note: The tongue shapes and presses the bolus back in the oral stage of swallowing.

parts.label: Extrinsic Muscles
parts.summary: The muscles that move the tongue from outside it
parts.function: Four pairs, from bone and the soft palate, protrude, retract, depress and raise the tongue. They change its position rather than its shape.

drives.note: The tongue pushes the bolus back against the palate in the oral stage of swallowing.

parts.label: Genioglossus
parts.summary: The fan-shaped muscle from the chin to the tongue
parts.function: It makes up most of the bulk of the tongue and pulls it forward and down.

parts.label: Hyoglossus
parts.summary: The muscle from the hyoid bone to the side of the tongue
parts.function: It pulls the sides of the tongue down.

parts.label: Styloglossus
parts.summary: The muscle from the styloid process to the side of the tongue
parts.function: It draws the tongue up and back.

parts.label: Palatoglossus
parts.summary: The muscle from the soft palate to the side of the tongue
parts.function: It lifts the back of the tongue and narrows the way into the throat. It lies in the palatoglossal arch.

parts.label: Nerves of the Tongue
parts.summary: The motor, sensory and taste nerves of the tongue
parts.function: One nerve moves the tongue. Others carry touch and taste from different parts of its surface.

parts.label: Hypoglossal Nerve (XII)
parts.summary: The motor nerve of the tongue
parts.function: It supplies the intrinsic muscles and all the extrinsic muscles except palatoglossus.

drives.note: Its motor fibres drive the tongue during swallowing.

parts.label: Lingual Nerve
parts.summary: The sensory nerve of the front of the tongue
parts.function: It carries touch, pain and temperature from the anterior two-thirds, and carries taste fibres from the chorda tympani.

parts.label: Chorda Tympani
parts.summary: A branch of the facial nerve that joins the lingual nerve
parts.function: It carries taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and parasympathetic fibres to the submandibular and sublingual glands.

parts.label: Glossopharyngeal Nerve (IX)
parts.summary: The nerve of taste and sensation for the back of the tongue
parts.function: It carries both taste and general sensation from the posterior third, including the vallate papillae.

parts.label: Teeth
parts.summary: Thirty-two permanent teeth set in the jaws
parts.function: Teeth are hard enamel-covered structures rooted in sockets of the upper and lower jaw. Incisors cut, canines tear, premolars and molars grind food before it is swallowed.

parts.label: Incisors
parts.summary: The chisel-shaped front teeth
parts.function: They cut food. There are two in each quarter of the jaw.

parts.label: Canines
parts.summary: The pointed teeth beside the incisors
parts.function: They tear food. There is one in each quarter of the jaw.

parts.label: Premolars
parts.summary: The two teeth between canine and molars in each quarter
parts.function: They crush and grind food.

parts.label: Molars
parts.summary: The three large back teeth in each quarter
parts.function: Their broad crowns grind food before it is swallowed.

parts.label: Oral Mucosa
parts.summary: The moist lining of the mouth
parts.function: It protects the tissue beneath and is kept wet by saliva. Its structure differs from region to region, being tougher where it is pressed by food.

parts.label: Buccal Mucosa
parts.summary: The lining of the cheeks
parts.function: It is soft and elastic so the cheek can move in chewing.

parts.label: Parotid Papilla
parts.summary: A small bump on the inside of the cheek
parts.function: The parotid duct opens here, opposite the upper second molar.

parts.label: Taste Bud (enlarged schematic)
parts.summary: An onion-shaped cluster of receptor cells, drawn magnified
parts.function: It is a microscopic organ, so this is a magnified diagram placed in the mouth, not at true size or position. Dissolved substances enter the pore and act on the receptor cells.

parts.label: Gustatory Receptor Cells
parts.summary: The taste-sensing cells
parts.function: They reach the pore with fine tips. When stimulated they excite the nerve fibres at their bases.

parts.label: Supporting Cells
parts.summary: The cells that surround the receptor cells
parts.function: They give the bud its shape and wrap the receptor cells.

parts.label: Basal Cells
parts.summary: Stem cells at the foot of the bud
parts.function: They replace the receptor and supporting cells, which wear out.

parts.label: Taste Pore
parts.summary: The small opening at the top of the bud
parts.function: Saliva and dissolved food reach the receptor cell tips through it.

parts.label: Gustatory Nerve Fibres
parts.summary: The nerve endings at the base of the bud
parts.function: They carry the signal from the receptor cells towards the brain.

parts.label: Tooth (enlarged molar, schematic)
parts.summary: One molar drawn magnified and in section
parts.function: This is a magnified diagram placed in the mouth, not at true size or position. It shows the layers common to every tooth.

parts.label: Crown
parts.summary: The part of the tooth above the gum
parts.function: It is the visible part that meets food and is covered by enamel.

parts.label: Neck
parts.summary: The narrow part where crown meets root
parts.function: It lies at the gum margin.

parts.label: Root
parts.summary: The part of the tooth set in the jaw
parts.function: It anchors the tooth in its socket. A molar has more than one root.

parts.label: Enamel
parts.summary: The hard white covering of the crown
parts.function: It is the hardest tissue of the body and resists wear.

parts.label: Dentine
parts.summary: The yellowish bone-like bulk of the tooth
parts.function: It lies under the enamel and the cementum and forms most of the tooth.

parts.label: Pulp Cavity
parts.summary: The soft core of the crown
parts.function: It holds nerves and vessels that nourish and sense the tooth.

parts.label: Gingival Sulcus
parts.summary: The shallow groove between gum and tooth
parts.function: It is the small gap at the gum margin around the neck.

parts.label: Root Canal
parts.summary: The channel of the pulp through the root
parts.function: It carries the pulp's nerves and vessels to the crown.

parts.label: Apical Foramen
parts.summary: The opening at the tip of the root
parts.function: Nerves and vessels enter the root canal through it.

parts.label: Cementum
parts.summary: The thin bony layer covering the root
parts.function: The fibres of the periodontal ligament attach to it.

parts.label: Periodontal Ligament
parts.summary: The fibrous sling between the root and its socket
parts.function: It holds the tooth in place and cushions it against the forces of chewing.

parts.label: Alveolar Bone
parts.summary: The bone of the jaw that forms the socket
parts.function: It surrounds the root and holds it.
